A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HD-Explain by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic demonstrations, qualitative and quantitative image-classification explanation experiments, kernel comparisons and CIFAR-10 data-debugging results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds SVHN evaluations and a CIFAR-10 failure-case analysis.

M1.justification: Equation 2 changes the label component of the reported Stein score from f_theta(x) to log f_theta(x), affecting the kernel's scoring definition. The kernel-ranking procedure and HD-Explain* construction remain. Appendix D still uses the earlier probability expression, so implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: v2 adds SVHN digit images to qualitative, augmentation-based retrieval and kernel-choice evaluations. The synthetic datasets, CIFAR-10, ovarian histopathology and brain MRI remain. This extends domain coverage within the existing image-classification explanation task.

E2.justification: The principal comparisons retain Influence Function, RPS and TracIn*. New Figure 10 additionally compares HD-Explain with standalone RBF similarity and an influence-based comparator labelled IF*. Standalone RBF similarity was not an evaluated explanation comparator in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix L introduces a diagnostic procedure that lowers the Stein-kernel selection threshold to inspect weakly relevant explanations. Existing ResNet-18 settings, last-layer comparator restrictions, noise injection, horizontal flipping and evaluation metrics are retained. The newly reported hardware is additional disclosure, not an established setting change.

E4.justification: Appendix L and Figure 10 add a qualitative investigation of raw-feature dependence and failures among weakly relevant explanations. The existing kernel-choice analysis extends to SVHN. Data debugging remains, while the medical qualitative comparison is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals, 30 augmented test points per training example and 30 independent data-debugging runs. v2 applies the existing uncertainty-reporting practice to additional results without reporting new statistical procedures or increased repetition counts.

E6.justification: Figures 4–7 add SVHN qualitative examples, retrieval scores, coverage, execution times and kernel comparisons. Figure 10 adds examples of weak or wrong-class explanatory support. The principal quantitative results on the original three image datasets and the data-debugging findings are largely retained; these additions do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds the input-marginal term to the KL decomposition and changes the stated KL–KSD derivative from differentiation with respect to theta to epsilon. Equation 2 revises the label-score derivation, and Section 3.1 explicitly identifies the continuous treatment of discrete labels as an approximation. These are localized mathematical revisions; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claims of precise, efficient, model-aware example explanations remain. The introduction drops the promise of a corresponding confidence level. The conclusion adds applicability to any layer and analysis of predictions across layers, while removing its earlier emphasis on data-debugging effectiveness.

C2.justification: Appendices E, F and L substantially expand the qualifications: KSD relaxations are restricted to the explanation context, visual medical similarity is distinguished from clinical validation, and unreliable explanations are linked to raw-feature similarity and model generalization. Section 4.2 also qualifies whole-model versus last-layer timing comparisons. The earlier intentional-bias misuse warning is replaced by an overreliance warning.

D1.justification: New Appendix I specifies a GTX 1080 Ti GPU, second-generation Ryzen 5 processor and 32 GB memory. Conversely, v1's explicit statement that code is available in supplementary materials disappears, although Table 2 retains 'Shared with code' entries. This changes documentation without establishing that code availability itself changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Molnar (2020), Kubokawa (2024) and Jitkrittum et al. (2020), supporting interpretable-model terminology, Stein-identity background and conditional-density motivation. It modestly revises the critique of prototype methods while retaining the broader positioning against influence-based explanations.

P1.justification: v2 adds an explicit contribution summary, revises portions of the method and evaluation exposition, and rewrites the conclusion. Medical qualitative discussion moves into the appendix, which receives dedicated discussion sections. The main section sequence and much of the existing narrative remain.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to a single-column layout. Synthetic figures are rearranged, the kernel comparison changes from a 2-by-2 grid to a horizontal strip, and benchmark plots gain SVHN groups and revised styling. The medical figure moves to Appendix F, while new SVHN and failure-case figures are added.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's brief caveats, v2 provides substantially clearer applicability limits and concrete failure examples; hardware disclosure also improves reproducibility. These support a modest overall gain in transparency. The gain is constrained by unresolved inconsistencies: Equation 2 uses log probabilities while Appendix D retains probabilities, and the newly reported SVHN horizontal-flip results differ substantially between Figures 6 and 7 without explanation.
